disputes.objection: A Three.js table with a lamp, depth of field, and a 14-second truck along the Highland Park photograph turns evidence into a diorama, and it softens the very non-Latin type we most need to be sharp when it is sampled as a texture. Even a 6 to 8 percent push is more movement than a viewer can tell apart from grading, and a lit surround invents a light source the archive never had. The motion belongs in the type and the line, driven by the narration, not in a virtual camera.
disputes.concession: KINETIC grants that the camera should arrive at the thing the narrator is about to name, and that a held photograph with a precise word landing on it is the strongest shot we have. A single slow move to a named detail, such as the words WRITTEN BY HIMSELF on the real title page, is allowed as a flat 2D move on unchanged pixels.

disputes.objection: A hanging shop lamp, raking sun and a gas lamp falling off across the surround is a grade by another name, because it tells the viewer where light came from in rooms we are not showing. A lamp that swells and dips on the narration's pulse is exactly the amber glow the Art Council just retired, only rendered in 3D. If a graphic has to move with the voice, let it be real feedback from the amplitude, not stagecraft laid on evidence.
disputes.concession: SIGNAL accepts CINEMATIC's Dead Air before the hardest facts, with real room tone and no music, and the idea that the pause is the honesty. SIGNAL also accepts a slow 2 percent push on a reconstruction, never on a photograph.

disputes.objection: A 3px raster, a tracking band and a 12px chromatic de-bleed read as a trend, a CRT costume, and they make our painted frames look like broken footage rather than a labelled argument. After H.264 on a phone that raster will moire and band, and rolling or tearing pictures near photosensitive viewers is a liability we cannot see from a desk. The label and the smaller frame already say reconstruction; the image does not also need to be damaged to prove it.
disputes.concession: CINEMATIC concedes that the surround and the type may carry the signal, that voice-amplitude can drive a very small thing like a rule's thickness, and that a build gate comparing archive pixels to their source scan, with a PSNR floor of 40 dB, is worth shipping.

disputes.objection: KINETIC's rule that nothing outruns the voice, with word-step luminance on captions and numbers popping at 1.25x, is a metronome, not acting; a stamp with no anticipation and no one-frame hold on impact has no weight. A word-by-word brightening is also the exact reveal the Art Council struck from the entrance. In a film about people who were enslaved or displaced, a plate that settles and then does nothing is the performance, and a held frame is a decision.
disputes.concession: CHARACTER grants that the whole film must be clocked to the narration's word-timing file, that cuts snap to the breath gaps, and that type should land on the spoken digit. CHARACTER will take KINETIC's 70 percent plain cuts if the stamps and locks that remain keep their weight.

disputes.objection: A 12-second opening, with 6 seconds of room tone and a key card, burns more than five percent of a 3 minute 40 second film before a word is spoken, and the Art Council already cut the exhibit entrance to about four seconds. Shadows and grain sampled from each plate's own light across four films is also a hand-matching job that, done carelessly, becomes a grade through the back door.
disputes.concession: KINETIC accepts COMPOSITOR's honesty key, the one line 'Real photographs first. Paintings are labelled.', and its rule that where a plate sits on a visible black rectangle the ground is matched to the plate and never the reverse.

disputes.objection: A flat ground and a hairline frame look clean, but a hard-edged rectangle on a flat colour is precisely the seam that makes graphics look added afterward, and it leaves the Persia seal sitting in a mismatched black box. If the ground, the type and the maps do not share the plate's black point and light direction, the premium feeling GENERATIVE wants is the first thing lost. Also, a procedural engine that refuses cuts is only as good as the evidence it is fed.
disputes.concession: COMPOSITOR concedes that a compiled rule, where the build refuses a direct archive-to-reconstruction cut, beats a promise to be careful, and that the sampled-value sheet per plate should be limited to the few plates that visibly need it.

disputes.objection: A constant takt that slides every scene on Ford, and a plain 20-frame cross-dissolve inside every Persia chapter, turns every cut into a transition, so the film never gets a hard cut that carries meaning. Our best default is the plain cut in the narrator's gap, about 70 percent of the time, and anything that moves must justify itself against that. Dissolves between plates are the slideshow look we are replacing.
disputes.concession: KINETIC grants that something should persist across the film: the Ford counter that advances one station per chapter, the Persia route that leads from room to room, the Partition margin line that thickens. These live as a margin device, not as a slide on every cut.

disputes.objection: Spending Magnific credits on generated sound effects for case rattle and time-clock ticks puts a synthetic, un-sourced sound on films whose entire promise is honest provenance. The only sound that earns a physical hit is one that was recorded or sourced as real, placed on the hold frame, and a generated tick will be heard as a stock whoosh. The hit is part of the acting, and it has to be a real object.
disputes.concession: CHARACTER lets generated audio fill a gap where no recording can be found, provided it is credited as generated on the end card, and accepts GENERATIVE's point that one stamp sound must be identical every time so the ear learns the label.

direction.frameSpec: 1920x1080, 30 fps, deterministic: every frame is a pure function render(t) of a timeline JSON (narration word timings, plate list with kind=archive or reconstruction, transition list, graphics list). Chromium renders all type through DOM so Syriac, Nastaliq, Devanagari, Gurmukhi and CJK shape correctly; SVG for rules, bars, counters and maps; WebGL only for ink or paper texture on type and ground, never on a photograph. The narration's forced-alignment word timing is the master clock, and the same JSON writes the SRT and WebVTT captions. Reduced-motion is an authored cut list (holds and 150 ms fades), not a disabled animation. Narration -16 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP.
direction.structure: About 3 minutes 35 seconds per film, in one shape for all four so they read as a family. 0:00 to 0:07 title sequence (below). Then five to six rooms of roughly 35 to 40 seconds each, matching the rooms on the exhibit's plan strip, each with one evidence plate held largest and one motion graphic or document moment; the Room Hairline across the bottom edge draws as progress and carries 'Room 3 of 6' so the film matches the exhibit. Each room: archive plate lands on a breath gap, narration states the claim, the caption band follows clause by clause, a lower third appears only on a first entrance of a person, place or date, and the room ends on a Breath Cut or its exhibit's chapter transition. Reconstructions never open or close a room; they sit in the middle, smaller and framed, and the plate they rest on is shown beside or immediately after. Ford's Beliefs and Morals room has the same length, type size, caption grammar and pace as the Rouge room, goes in through a Silence Hold, and uses the real printed Dearborn Independent pages, each held at least 4 seconds with nothing animated over them. The last 12 seconds are an end card: a provenance ledger (for example 'archive photographs, documents, reconstructions (all labelled)') with each credit at 24px or larger, the translators and native readers who proofed non-Latin text, and the fonts and sources.
direction.titleSequence: About 6.5 seconds, skippable by any key, tap or remote button, with Play live from frame one. 0.0 to 0.4 s: flat exhibit ground, room tone only. 0.4 to 2.2 s: one real, ungraded archive plate arrives at full size on its real edges with its credit under it (Douglass daguerreotype on its real oval and mat, the Highland Park line photograph, the Xi'an stele rubbing or British Museum seal, a 1947 station or luggage photograph), no blur backdrop. 2.2 to 4.6 s: the title is set whole, in the margin column, never across a face, by the exhibit's own gesture: Douglass sets FREDERICK DOUGLASS sort by sort into a composing stick (18 frames, last sort landing on the first narration word), Ford stamps HENRY FORD and the line in two thuds eight frames apart, Persia draws the lapis line and then sets the title in Cormorant with real Syriac and the stele characters faded behind in the empty third, Partition draws the madder line and sets the title in Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi and English at equal weight and cap height. 4.6 to 6.5 s: one slate line in the system sans ('A Plajah Dossier film, 3 min 35 s, captions on'), the Room Hairline draws in, the honesty line 'Real photographs first. Paintings are labelled.' sets for 1.5 s, and a content-note chip appears where the film needs one (Partition and the martyrdom beat of Persia). No year counter, no word-by-word reveal, no letterbox bars, no lens flare, no logo animation. Narration starts under the last half second.

transitionKit.name: Breath Cut
transitionKit.use: The default, about 65 percent of all cuts: a hard cut between plates inside a room, and into and out of every document. Nothing else may be used if this works.
transitionKit.timing: Cut lands 3 frames after the last phoneme of a clause, inside a narration gap of 120 ms or more. No effect, no sound. Never inside a spoken word.

transitionKit.name: Stamp Slam
transitionKit.use: Ford chapter changes in Motor City and the War Effort only, three or four per film, always on a spoken year or number.
transitionKit.timing: A #ff4b1f stencil bar 160px tall slams across in 6 frames, holds 4 frames (the one-frame hold on impact is inside this), strikes out in 6 frames, 16 frames total; plate swaps under it on frame 7. One dry steel tap on the impact frame. Not used in the Beliefs room.

transitionKit.name: Forme Lock
transitionKit.use: Douglass chapter changes, about four per film. The type of the next room's title is set after the lock.
transitionKit.timing: Four gold hairline rules close inward on the incoming plate's rectangle over 10 frames with a one-frame overshoot, hold 6 frames, open over 10; old plate drops out on frame 5. Soft wood-on-metal thump on the lock frame. Title sorts then set over 18 frames.

transitionKit.name: Road Line
transitionKit.use: Persia, only when the story changes place (Ctesiphon, Merv, Chang'an). The same line is the Room Hairline and later the route map.
transitionKit.timing: A lapis hairline already across the frame becomes the seam; the old image exits left and the new enters right along it over 24 frames, ease-in-out, with the ghost script behind drifting at 0.3x counter-parallax. A single plucked string at the start of the line only.

transitionKit.name: Madder Rule
transitionKit.use: Partition, only for place changes and for the moment the Radcliffe line is drawn, two or three per film so it keeps its force. Never on a face, a refugee photograph or violence.
transitionKit.timing: A 4px madder line is drawn top to bottom in 18 frames with hand irregularity; the image on one side changes first, the other 6 frames later. Pencil scratch sound, otherwise silence. The line then stays as a 3px margin hairline for the rest of the film.

transitionKit.name: Reconstruction Gate
transitionKit.use: Every archive-to-reconstruction move in all four films. The build refuses to compile a direct cut.
transitionKit.timing: The archive plate cuts to bare exhibit ground for 10 frames; the RECONSTRUCTION stamp and its one-line evidence note are set first (the same identical thunk every time), then the painting fades up over 12 frames, smaller and inside a hairline frame; the label stays for the entire time the painting is on screen. The return to archive is a 2-frame hard snap to full-size plate with the label gone, the cleanest cut in the film.

transitionKit.name: Silence Hold
transitionKit.use: Before distressing or contested material: Partition violence and displacement photographs, Persia's martyrdom account, Douglass's account of the whip, and the Ford Beliefs and Morals room and the Dearborn Independent pages.
transitionKit.timing: Music out 30 frames before, a plain content card in the exhibit face with real room tone (never digital silence) held 45 frames, then a hard cut to the document or photograph. No ink, line, stamp, push or particle. Viewer can skip the section with any key.

transitionKit.name: Ground Dip
transitionKit.use: Time passing inside one subject (Douglass boyhood to escape) and the end of every film into the credit ledger.
transitionKit.timing: 12 frames to the exhibit's own ground colour (never black or white) and 12 back; at film end the last plate dims to its own scan edge over 18 frames beneath the final line and the ledger rises. No black dip anywhere mid-film.

direction.typography: One display face per exhibit, one shared body serif, one shared system sans, all browser-rendered, all SIL OFL. Ford: Anton caps, 168 to 220px titles, 64px numerals and place names, line-height 0.92, #ff4b1f only on type and rules (never as a fill behind a photograph). Douglass: Abril Fatface 120 to 190px titles in mixed case, Alfa Slab One 56 to 96px for dates and single shouted words (set as a handbill stack: three sizes, ragged centre axis), gold #d9b36a only on type and hairline rules, never as a wash. Persia: Cormorant Garamond 500 and italic, 110 to 150px, lapis #4f7cff on midnight; real Estrangela Syriac (Noto Sans Syriac Eastern) and Noto Serif SC for the stele at 420 to 700px, 8 to 12 percent opacity, set in the empty third and never behind a plate or the title, and set legible at 64px beside the English whenever a name is spoken. Partition: Fraunces 600 (SOFT 0, WONK 0) 130 to 170px, madder #e8553d only on the drawn line and years; Noto Nastaliq Urdu (line-height 2.0), Noto Serif Devanagari, Noto Serif Gurmukhi at matched optical size, order stable across the film. Shared: Source Serif 4 Text 600 at 44px for captions; Inter Tight 500 at 26 to 28px for provenance, room, credit and years with tabular figures; RECONSTRUCTION is the only tracked caps in the family (Inter Tight caps, +140 tracking, 30px, hollow 3px #ff6b57 box). No tiny tracked gold caps, no ghost numerals, no fake bold on scripts, no Nastaliq in a Latin box. Hex values above are starting points: read the final tokens from the live exhibit CSS so film and exhibit match pixel for pixel. Every accent colour must pass 4.5:1 on its ground; nudge lapis lighter if it does not.
direction.captionsAndLowerThirds: No box, no pill, no translucent anything. A fixed layout on a 3:2 module reserves three zones so text can never touch evidence: the evidence field (top 72 percent of the frame, y 0 to about 790) holds the plate on the left two thirds and a flat margin column on the right third for year, place and the Provenance Slate; the caption band (bottom 22 percent, 9 percent safe margin) holds captions in Source Serif 4 at 44px, two lines maximum, about 60 characters a line, sentence case. Captions are phrase-chunked from the alignment file, one chunk per spoken clause, entering 2 frames before the first word's onset and leaving 6 frames after the last word, hard swap, no fade longer than 4 frames, ceiling about 14 characters per second. The word being spoken sits at 100 percent luminance, the rest at 70 percent (no karaoke colour, no bounce, no scale); this can be turned off in the player. Names, dates and numbers spoken in the narration are set in the exhibit's accent colour at the same size and weight, with no size jump. The Provenance Slate is always present under the plate's left edge for the full hold at 26px minimum, two lines: ARCHIVE in plain ink with institution, year, licence, or the RECONSTRUCTION stamp plus one 28px line saying what is evidence and what is imagined. Lower third is one structure: a 2px accent rule 48px long draws left to right in 10 frames, a name or place in the exhibit's display face at 56px, role and date in Inter Tight 28px; holds at least 3 seconds, retracts in 6 frames, appears only on a first entrance of a person, place or date and at most once per 25 seconds, never over a face or on a distressing plate. Gated material gets a plain card first ('The next section describes violence. Skip with any key.'), never a lower third. Sidecar SRT and VTT use the same chunking so captions-off keeps the structure.
infographics: FORD, chassis clock: two Anton bars on one belt, 750 minutes in grey (40 frames) versus 93 minutes in #ff4b1f (8 frames) to true scale (the short bar is 12.4 percent of the long), numeral counting with ratchet ticks, landing on the spoken word 'ninety-three', 93 held 2 seconds. It sits beside the Highland Park line photograph and does not cover it.

FORD, Five Dollar Day: two stacked wage tokens to scale, about $2.34 versus $5.00, labelled 'reported 1914 daily wage' with the source line; the figures are verified against the exhibit's cited source before render.

FORD, Model T counter: seven-digit ledger counter or 150-square chassis grid (each square about 100,000 cars) reaching about 15 million over one sentence, ending on a stencilled 'ABOUT'; uses real dated production figures from the cited source and never an invented curve.

DOUGLASS, Narrative title page call-out: the real 1845 scan held full and still; a 2px gold underline draws once under the actual words WRITTEN BY HIMSELF in 14 frames as the narration says it, then a flat crop-in on unchanged pixels; nothing retyped over the page.

DOUGLASS, handbill timeline: c. 1818 (the last digit left as a blank quad, because he never knew his birthday), 1838 and 1845 set in wood-type slab with ABOUT on the first; the real North Star masthead shown as a plate; a thin gold route line from Baltimore to New York, September 1838, on a plain schematic.

PERSIA, the road map: a vector map from Natural Earth or GeoNames geometry, a lapis route from Seleucia-Ctesiphon (410) to Chang'an (635, 781), drawn at constant speed with a stop at each named city, English plus real Syriac or Chinese at the same size; documented segments solid, traditional or uncertain segments dashed, and the whole labelled 'schematic route'.

PERSIA, the stele: the real inscription held, the narrator reads the date, the real characters light in reading order (top to bottom for Chinese) and 781 resolves from them, never typed over them; translator credited with it.

PARTITION, the Line: the 1947 boundary drawn as one madder line across a flat soot map (reusing public/dossier/partition-map.html geometry) over about 6 seconds as the narrator reads, place names in Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi, English; labelled schematic where the geometry is approximate.

PARTITION, the range bar: displacement and deaths shown as ranges with soft ends and the words 'estimates differ' in the sans, using only the exhibit's own cited figures, never a rolling total, a body-count ticker, a red flash or a dot swarm; one static draw, no animation beyond it.
PARTITION, date stack: 3 June, 14, 15 and 17 August 1947 set as stacked Fraunces lines with the madder underline moving between them.

Rules for every graphic: a number animates only if the narration says it first and a source line is on screen; each is real vector so it stays sharp on a TV; each is under about 4 seconds on screen except the route and the Line; none is composited into or over a photograph; at most three kinetic-type moments per film, each on a spoken date or number that is the beat of the story, and no kinetic type on suffering.
direction.gradeAndTexture: Archive photographs are only ever positioned, scaled and masked: no grade, no tint, no violet-sepia, no vignette, no blur backdrop, no film grain, no halation, no AI upscaling, no depth-map parallax, no tonal change except dust removal on the scan with a before and after check. They are shown at their real edges (daguerreotype oval and brass mat, plate border) at 60 to 72 percent of frame height, on a flat exhibit-colour ground with a 1px hairline frame; a plate is never smaller than any reconstruction in the same shot. Where a plate sits on a visible black rectangle (the Persia seal) the ground's black point is matched to the plate, never the plate to the ground. Texture (letterpress paper tooth, ink gain on type, rubbing-ink edge) lives on the ground and the type only, at 4 percent or less, never inside the photograph rectangle. Camera: a linear drift of at most 3 percent over a hold only where the narration points at a region of interest, never on a distressing plate; and at most two flat 'detail moves' per film into unchanged pixels of a document or title page, with the whole plate shown first and the slate saying 'detail'; no push-in on a refugee or violence photograph, no whip pan, no zoom blur, no light leak, no glitch. Reconstructions are smaller than the plate, inside a hairline frame with the RECONSTRUCTION stamp and evidence note present from first frame to last, may take a 2 percent push, and are never animated as video; faceless and back-turned paintings only. Build gates: decode locked frames, crop every archive plate region and fail the build if PSNR against the scaled source crop is below 40 dB; fail if any reconstruction frame lacks its stamp; fail on any caption or lower-third bounding box that overlaps a plate; flash check under 3 flashes per second.

perExhibit.douglass: The composing stick and the handbill. Iron-gall brown-black ground, gold only on type and rules, Abril Fatface with slab dates; titles and the pull-quotes set sort by sort on the narration, chapter changes by Forme Lock; the hero moments are real documents, the 1845 Narrative title page and the North Star masthead. The mustard blur is deleted, the faced lectern and study paintings are cut and replaced with real photographs or engravings, and the faceless boy-chalking-a-plank painting carries the early rooms under its label. Calm authority, no fanfare, and a Silence Hold before the account of violence.
perExhibit.ford: The stencil and the line. Iron ground, signal red-orange only on stencilled numerals, tags and rules, Anton caps, one stamp sound that recurs; the Highland Park line photograph is the longest-held and largest plate, with the 750-to-93 chassis clock beside it. Ford himself is a photograph or seen from behind, never a painted hero; the back-turned Quadricycle and the boy at the bench stay, labelled. The Beliefs and Morals room is built in the identical type and caption grammar, enters through a Silence Hold, and shows the real printed Dearborn Independent masthead and pages dated, with no red stamp, no sync, no lamp and no music swell; a Jewish museum partner reviews it before the film ships.
perExhibit.persia: The road and the script. Midnight ground, lapis only (no amber, no gold, so it is not Douglass), Cormorant italic, real Syriac and Chinese script large and faded in the empty third and legible when it is the subject. The slowest film of the family: longest holds, wide easing, a 24-frame Road Line that is also the Room Hairline and later the route map. The British Museum seal sits as a real photograph, big, on a ground matched to its black, with its credit set properly; paintings are places and objects only. A Silence Hold and a held 'historians debate' line before the martyrdom passage.
perExhibit.partition: The line. Soot ground, madder only on the drawn line and years, Fraunces, the title in Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi and English at equal weight proofed by named native readers (if proof is not in hand, the title ships English-only rather than wrong). One gesture: a line is drawn, hesitates, divides the frame, and stays as a margin hairline that thickens each room. Real photographs only for people; reconstructions are empty places (a platform, a signed map table), never faces; refugee and violence photographs sit behind a content note and Silence Hold, full size, ungraded, no push-in, nothing animated, captions below.

direction.sound: The narration's word timing is the master clock: text enters 2 frames before its word's onset, counters land on the spoken digit, no transition may begin inside a spoken word. Score is one sparse bed per film (60 to 72 BPM or beatless), ducked 8 to 10 dB under voice with a 12-frame attack, and drops out at every Silence Hold. Sound design is physical, real and about 20 dB under voice: a dry steel tap and ratchet ticks (Ford), a platen thump and type-in-stick clicks (Douglass), a single plucked string and wind (Persia), pencil on map and room tone (Partition), and one identical thunk for the RECONSTRUCTION stamp across all four films. Foley sits on the hold frame of the impact, not the first frame of the move. Real room tone, never digital silence.

synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: CHARACTER's weight: every authored move has anticipation, an arc, a one-frame hold on impact and a settle, and exits run at about 70 percent of the entry time; the archive plate never animates its pixels, only its mount settles; the animation vocabulary goes quiet exactly where the material gets heavy (Beliefs, martyrdom, Partition violence, the whip), and that contrast is the point; the Beat-Cut (hard cut on a score downbeat to a plate half-seen in a corner for 12 frames) allowed twice per film at most; real foley placed on the hold frame; and an authored reduced-motion cut list per film.
synthesis.editorCut: GENERATIVE cut: the 3D lit table, shop lamps and depth of field (CINEMATIC); the 3px raster, tracking bands, 12px chromatic de-bleed and voice-driven wobble (SIGNAL); plate-sampled grain, plate-sampled shadows and the 12-second opening with a 6-second silent lead-in (COMPOSITOR); the per-scene takt slide and Persia's within-chapter cross-dissolve (GENERATIVE's own proposals, because a transition on every cut is the slideshow again); squash-and-stretch on stamps beyond a 2 percent overshoot (CHARACTER); the 1.25x size jump on spoken numbers and word-by-word reveals (KINETIC); the Persia 'bell and wind' sound clichés; the live DOM version of the engine in v1 (ship the baked MP4 and VTT first); and every generated graphic, background, ink or smoke. What survives is a type-and-line film on flat exhibit grounds with held, ungraded photographs, a few gestures that carry weight, and a build that refuses to compile a dishonest cut.
synthesis.productionPlan:
In order. 1) Tokens: pull colour, type and spacing values from the live exhibit CSS into one tokens file exported as JSON and shared with Tela, so a type spec is single-sourced. 2) Narration timing: use the platform's TTS timing endpoint for the Aria narration or forced alignment for a human voice, and build a beat map per film (clause onsets, stressed names and numbers, gaps of 120 ms or more). 3) Plates (Pillow): highest-resolution source scans (Library of Congress, Wikimedia, British Museum), cropped to real edges, credit lines in data, dust cleaning only, contact sheets; a sampled black-point entry only for plates that visibly need it. 4) Film Engine (HTML, CSS, SVG, small WebGL for type texture, rendered frame by frame by Playwright at 30 fps) with the shared kit: caption chunker, Provenance Slate, Room Hairline, lower third, label-gate compiler (refuses a direct archive-to-reconstruction cut), the PSNR and overlap gates, and four exhibit modules so a fifth exhibit is a config. 5) Lottie or dotLottie, authored once, for the reusable gestures that also live in the app (RECONSTRUCTION stamp, stamp slam, line draw, lock rules, caption rule); not for title sequences. 6) Tela: title cards, end-card ledgers and the static vector infographics from the tokens JSON. 7) Fabula: the assembly bench for narration, score, foley, ducking, loudness and the captions track, and the FX preview for the owner's review of the timeline. 8) Magnific, last and only where it earns its cost. 9) Render per chapter in four parallel workers, concat with hard joins, encode with ffmpeg (x264 CRF 16, yuv420p, bt709, +faststart, optional ProRes mezzanine), write SRT and VTT, then run all gates. 10) Human gates before publish: native readers named for every Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi, Syriac and Chinese string (English-only if not proofed), the honesty checklist (every plate has a slate, every number sourced), parity check that the Ford Beliefs room matches the Rouge room in type size and pace, and a Jewish museum partner review of the Dearborn Independent material.

Magnific cost note: I have not priced these, so run the account's cost simulation before spending; roughly, stills and short sound clips are cheap relative to video, and the expected spend is a modest batch: about 15 to 25 faceless still reconstructions in total (replacing the faced Douglass lectern and study paintings and Ford's folded-arms painting with faceless or back-turned versions, plus any missing empty-place scenes for Partition), four to six flat texture plates (iron, handbill paper, rag paper, soot) for the ground only, and only if real recordings cannot be found, about 10 to 20 short sound-effect clips. Image upscaling only as a labelled, before-and-after-checked fix for a scan that fails resolution, and never silently.

What NOT to generate: any video of any person or any animated painting (an invented face in motion); any new face for Douglass, Ford, Persia's clergy or Partition's people; any morph between a photograph and a painting; depth-map parallax or AI upscaling applied to archive; generated title backgrounds, ink, smoke or light leaks; generated Syriac, Chinese, Urdu, Hindi or Punjabi text or translation; any imagery of the Beliefs material, the whip, the martyrdom or Partition violence; generated archive-looking photographs; and generated narration of a historical figure's own words. Generate sound last, credited as generated, only after sourcing real recordings.
synthesis.openDecision: Will you accept that in these films no painting ever goes full-bleed, with every reconstruction smaller and framed and the cinema coming from type, the drawn line and held photographs, or do you want exactly one labelled full-bleed painting per film (starting with Ford's B-24) as the single exception, knowing it will be the most impressive frame and also the least evidenced?
synthesis.ariaSummary: The six directors agreed on almost everything that matters. Every film gets one fixed layout, the real photograph stays the largest thing on screen and is never touched, every painting is labelled and smaller, and the old blurred background and the tiny credit in the corner are gone. They also agreed that each exhibit needs its own look and motion: Ford is stamped, Douglass is set in type, Persia is drawn along a road, and Partition is a line that divides the screen. They split on how much cinema to add. Some wanted a 3D table with lamps and camera moves, some wanted a signal-and-glitch treatment, and some wanted heavy weight and hand-acted gestures. I chose the type-and-line approach as the base, kept the sense of weight and quiet on the hardest moments from the character director, and cut the lamps, the glitches and the fancy transitions on every cut. The one question for you is whether you will allow one full-screen painting per film, or hold the line that no painting ever goes full screen.

reflections.note: I gave up the metronome: I now accept the weight and settle on a stamp and the rule that heavy material gets nothing at all, which is truer to how a type-led film should feel. I still hold that a 3D table and a lamp are the wrong place to spend a film's attention.

I gave way on holds being timed to the narration and on plain cuts being the default, because the weight lands harder against that quiet. I still hold that the gestures that remain need an arc and a settle, and that the gesture goes silent exactly where the subject is hardest.

I let go of plate-sampled shadows and grain, which would have become a grade by the back door across four films. I still want the ground matched to the plate where a mismatch shows, like the Persia seal's black rectangle, and I want the PSNR gate on every plate before anything ships.

Taking the editor's chair meant cutting several of my own proposals, including the per-scene takt slide and the live version for the first release. I still hold that a build which refuses to compile an archive-to-reconstruction cut without its label is the real safeguard, not our good intentions.

I dropped the raster, the tracking bands and the de-bleed on paintings; after phones and photosensitivity checks, a hollow frame and a stamp say the same thing more safely. I kept the idea that picture fidelity is provenance, and the PSNR gate and flash check that prove it.

I gave up the 3D table and the lamps, and I accept that my 6 to 8 percent push is too much against a photograph. What I still hold is that the camera should arrive at the thing before the word names it, and that Dead Air with real room tone before the hardest facts is where these films will feel most like cinema.
